math_plain: Compress example information into a learnable code that you inject into each layer of a frozen language model to improve time-series forecasting.
why_math: It works because compressing examples into a focused code lets you steer the model's existing knowledge toward a new task without retraining. The model already learned general patterns; you just show it which examples matter for this specific forecast.

math_plain: Use a similarity score (cosine) to measure how close a generated voice is to a reference voice, optimizing until they sound the same.
why_math: It works because voices that sound alike to humans also sit close together in acoustic space—the same properties that make them audibly similar also make their numbers geometrically close. Measuring distance is faster and more reliable than human listening.

math_plain: Iteratively rewrite news queries to retrieve better evidence for fact-checking, optimizing queries based on feedback from a detector.
why_math: It works because the query that retrieves the most useful evidence is usually not the original words. By learning to translate news into effective search terms—using feedback on which evidence actually helped—you align retrieval with verification needs.

math_plain: Score node importance in a network, then craft fake identities to hide a true node's importance—evading detection based on network structure.
why_math: It works because network importance measures rely on connection patterns; an adversary can exploit this by creating many fake identities and distributing connections in ways that obscure their true network position. The ranking algorithm cannot tell real influence from orchestrated noise.

math_plain: Select the most informative log patterns under a false-alarm budget, then grind them into rules that catch anomalies with minimal false alarms.
why_math: It works because anomalies are rare and distinctive—the patterns that help you catch them are also the ones that reduce confusion. By optimizing which patterns matter most while keeping false positives bounded, you trade recall against reliability in a controlled way.

math_plain: Generate synthetic fake transaction patterns to rehearse spotting old fraud types, preventing a model from forgetting as new patterns emerge.
why_math: It works because streaming fraud detection faces catastrophic forgetting—as new scams arise, models unlearn old ones. Replaying synthetic historical fraud patterns keeps the old detectors sharp without storing real data, which is impossible at scale.

why_math: It works because models trained on Western data absorb Western meanings. By measuring performance separately per culture and prompting in native languages, you expose how much detection relies on cultural cues the model never saw, revealing when translation erases meaning.

why_math: It works because emotions reveal themselves differently across modalities—speech tone and facial expression sometimes disagree with words. why_math: It works because the more a person clings to their own opinion, the more weight it carries in the group consensus. By tweaking how much each person sticks to their view, you reshape who influences the crowd—targeting minimal changes that rebalance power between groups.

math_plain: Train once on a data representation, then insert different fairness adapters at test time to tune fairness level without retraining.
why_math: It works because fairness is a tuning knob, not a fixed property. By learning a shared representation once and plugging in different fairness tweaks later, you avoid the cost of retraining while guaranteeing that fairness improves smoothly as you adjust the dial—each step is strictly more fair than the last.

math_plain: Extract structured concepts (symbols representing visual and rhetorical ideas) from images, then train a transparent model on those concepts to detect vaccine misinfo.
why_math: It works because concepts are interpretable—you can see exactly which visual cues (a syringe plus angry face plus text warning) triggered a detection. By grounding detection in human-understandable concepts rather than opaque scores, you get decisions you can audit and explain, making mistakes obvious and correctable.
